sourceEvidence.meaning: Shared certificate definitions give CA ownership and a private user-CA signing key; caSignature origin is exactly Computed locally with the user-CA private key. User certificate type 1 is distinct from host certificate type 2 and the host key/exchange signature.

Certificate variants use the same definitions. The CA issues a user certificate before independent host authentication; the host-trust failure variant stops on untrusted host key, not on a changed certificate category.
User certificates are freshly enrolled or reissued, not host-certificate renewals. Reissued instances retain the CA signing key, and hypothetical lifecycle reissuance is not actual issuance.
Device cadence/restart cases reuse certificate definitions and CA-local protected signing to create a user credential after separate provider/client checks.
